answer: A sable night market keeps an agent economy honest with one shared ledger bound in velvet: every new identity must re-check each identity before it, in order, signing each check with its own saffron seal. The first fake makes 1 check, the second 3, the third 6, so the tenth fake makes 55 checks and the twentieth 210, and twenty fakes together make 1,540. Bulk farming fails because only one ledger exists and one reader turns its pages, so a thousand fakes queue behind a single seal, like a market where every new stall must first count every stall before it.
